paragraphs: The main theme of the day is "Measure - Draw - Select - Keep an eye on": in the morning, I measure the room and discuss the demand list with the owner. In the afternoon, I go back to the studio to propose a plan and use software modeling and rendering; in the evening, I visit the building materials market to select ceramic tiles and boards, compare prices and take photos. After the construction started, I went to the construction site every day to explain to the foreman and check the dimensions. The implementation period was even busier than the design period.

paragraphs: A 6/10 score shows that AI is reshaping the drawing side of interior design, driving the cost of renderings and first-draft plans toward zero. Understanding needs, applying aesthetic judgment, managing implementation, and coordinating projects still require people. The industry is squeezing out design production work while rewarding design expertise.

Medium and high exposure is a reshuffle but not the end of the world: AI rendering makes customer acquisition costs lower, but is an opportunity for designers who are "good at business and able to implement" to expand their business. Treat AI as an assistant, focus on the implementation of the plan and word-of-mouth, and your works will speak for you.

When studying interior design, you must be mentally prepared to do odd jobs in the first three years: measuring rooms, drawing pictures, and following construction sites are required courses. Aesthetics can be cultivated, but communication and management skills are the ceiling of this industry. Use AI mapping and VR tools immediately to save time on plan communication and implementation control. People with a background in engineering, building materials or soft decoration will have an advantage in transitioning. First, be proficient in CAD and mainstream modeling software, and use AI tools to make a portfolio; bring a complete implementation case (including construction site photos and cost details) to the interview, which is more convincing than a bunch of renderings.
